text: Eight in a hundred people on food stamps in this country lost them inside six months, and they didn't stop being hungry when the help stopped. I'll widen that program so more families get food on the table, and I'll say plainly that a job and a decent living are partly this government's business too. I won't apologize for one dollar of it, and I'm not going to be talked out of it either. Not one dollar. And I approve this message.

A power company boss took home more than thirteen million dollars last year while his company stood in front of the regulators asking to raise your bill. I'll tax the people at that end harder, move some of that money down to the households falling behind, and leave every welfare program funded exactly where it is today. Nobody is cutting a dime out of them while I'm around, and they can put that in writing. Not one dime. And I approve this message.

The welfare block grant out of Washington hasn't moved since 1996. The same number every single year, worth forty percent less now than it was then. I'll cut welfare spending down hard, and I'll hand what is left straight to the family that came up short this month, in cash, in their own hands. No agencies. No forms. Nobody standing in the middle of it taking a cut off the top. And I approve this message.

Prices are still going up and you feel it every single week at the register. The Federal Reserve cut rates three times and hasn't moved since, and your grocery bill didn't care. I'm going to cut what goes out the door as aid to the poor, and I want this government out of the business of evening up what your neighbor has against what you have. Quit pretending it works. And I approve this message.

The tariff on steel and aluminum has sat at fifty percent the whole way through this year. Fifty percent. The people who study this will tell you it puts work into the places that make the steel and takes it back out of the places that buy it. That's as far as anybody ever gets. Nobody has had to say which of those two he meant to happen, and I'd like to hear one of them try. And I approve this message.

Thirty years in prison for a murder he didn't commit, and then the prosecutors dropped the case and walked off without a word to him. In Congress I'll pull our courts back off the people they are grinding up, and I'll go after the police violence and the racism under it. When a neighborhood goes up, force has never once fixed the thing that lit it. Nobody has even tried the other way. And I approve this message.

One city paid out more than six and a half million dollars over the protests of 2020, and a federal judge had to order its own officers to quit firing tear gas at people who weren't fighting anybody. That is what puts a street on fire. I'm for the death penalty for a murderer who earns it, and I'm going straight at the beatings and the bigotry that set those blocks off. No more force. And I approve this message.

One drug court in this country has been at this thirty years, and about five in a hundred who finish it ever offend again. Automatic prison over a handful of pills has never kept one man straight. I will take those mandatory drug sentences off the books in my first year, and a felon still doesn't earn his ballot back on the way out of the gate. Thirty years of proof is sitting there. Somebody use it. And I approve this message.

They shot Dedrick Robinson dead, and the man they charged with his murder was allowed to plead the whole thing down to reckless homicide. Five years of community control. Not one day behind bars. Every mandatory minimum stays on the books while I'm there, and a man who commits a felony in this country never votes again, not the day he walks out and not twenty years later. No more sweetheart deals. And I approve this message.

The Justice Department awarded nearly two hundred ninety million dollars for public safety. Read what the announcement says it covers: drug task forces, school officers, drug courts, new technology. A little of everything and nothing you can put your finger on. Ask them what it bought where you live and they'll mail you the press release again. I want the receipts, and I'll keep asking until somebody hands them over. And I approve this message.

They locked up a hospital chaplain for seventy-three days and told a court he was wanted overseas for murder, and then the government dropped the whole case. Now they want to run that on every family in this country without papers, and I'm fighting the mass deportations every step of the way. I'm also not going to stand here and pretend illegal immigration is what's driving crime in America. That's why I'm running. And I approve this message.

Fourteen million people are in this country illegally right now, the most there has ever been, and it didn't get that way by accident. In Congress I'll vote to tighten up that border, and I'll vote to keep people who came here illegally out of our local elections, every town hall and every school board in America. Lawmakers have had that number in front of them for years and sat on it. Enough talk. And I approve this message.

A woman under a deportation order went into federal court to stop it, five years after her case was turned down, and what she held up to the judge was her nine-year-old boy, born here, a citizen. A child born here doesn't buy his parents a pass. Neither does a wedding ring, and I mean to put an end to both of those claims for good. Carry out the order the court already gave her. And I approve this message.

Cameron Lyon was twenty-three. A car crossed the center line and killed him, and Homeland Security says the driver had been deported six years earlier and walked right back in, charged now with doing it drunk and with no license. The numbers coming across are out of control and I'm done being reasonable about it. That's why I'm fighting to put every last one of them on a plane home. Do it now. And I approve this message.

Thirty-nine members of the House put their names on an immigration bill. Thirty-nine names, and the thing is still just a bill. Signing your name costs a man nothing, and in that building it passes for the job. You've called that office, you've written the letters, and what came back was a form letter thanking you for your interest. I've run out of patience for people who are never in a hurry. And I approve this message.
